title: Saktah in the recitation of Hafs: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y10 lesson 30 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Saktah in the recitation of Hafs rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 30. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Saktah
points: A pause of about two counts
Marked with a small س (ۜ) in the Madinah mushaf

head: Where
After
Why it matters
rows: So 'upright' (qayyiman) is not heard as describing the 'crookedness'
Separates the words of those raised from the reply
Keeps «مَنْ رَاقٍۢ» as two words, not one sound

arabic.text: قَالُوا۟ يَٰوَيْلَنَا مَنۢ بَعَثَنَا مِن مَّرْقَدِنَا ۜ ۗ هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَصَدَقَ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ (٥٢)

head: Not this
This
rows: Taking a full breath at the saktah, or ignoring it and joining
Stop the voice briefly with no breath, then continue

keywords.def: a transmitted way of recitation, such as Hafs 'an 'Asim
stopping on a word, with a breath

questions.q: Recite 36:52 with the saktah, then 75:27 with the saktah.
questions.a: marqadinaa (saktah) haadhaa ...; wa qeela man (saktah) raaq.

questions.q: Pupil PDF: explain each saktah in a sentence and practise them aloud. Today's rota group recites Ya-Sin 37 to 52.
Extend: the sign ۗ also follows the saktah in 36:52. What does it allow?
questions.a: Stopping is better: a reciter may stop fully there instead of the saktah.

questions.q: Stretch: why does merging «مَنْ رَاقٍۢ» without a saktah sound like one word?
questions.a: Noon sakinah before ر would merge (idgham), making 'marraaq'; the saktah keeps the noon clear.
A) a short pause without breath. That is the definition used in Hafs.

questions.q: How many saktat are there in the recitation of Hafs (by ash-Shatibiyyah)?
Think again: A saktah is a pause with no breath. Why might a pause that short still matter for the meaning?
questions.a: It separates ideas or speakers that could otherwise run together, as in 36:52.
